$comment: Controlled corpus for verification/conformance-harness/conformance-harness.mjs. It retains the package-2 synthetic self-check pairs and, from package 4, includes a real Node.js/Rust source-format comparison. "$NODE" in a producer's "command" is resolved by runCorpus() to the interpreter running the harness itself; "cwd" is resolved relative to this file's own directory. Every case is run through the exact same runProducer/normalizeDiagnostics/compareVerdicts/runCase path CI, hooks/pre-push and test/conformance-harness.test.mjs use.

cases.name: identical-exit-and-diagnostics
cases.description: Same exit code, same FAIL and WARN messages, same order on both sides.

args: process.stdout.write('FAIL  missing required field: name\nWARN  deprecated flag --legacy used\n');process.exit(1);
process.stdout.write('FAIL  missing required field: name\nWARN  deprecated flag --legacy used\n');process.exit(1);

cases.name: same-diagnostics-different-order
cases.description: Two FAIL messages present on both sides, emitted in opposite order — order must not create a false divergence.

args: process.stdout.write('FAIL  field a is missing\nFAIL  field b is missing\n');process.exit(1);
process.stdout.write('FAIL  field b is missing\nFAIL  field a is missing\n');process.exit(1);

cases.name: different-exit-code
cases.description: Identical diagnostics, but the two sides exit with different codes.

cases.name: missing-fail-on-right
cases.description: Left reports two FAILs, right reports only one of them — a dropped FAIL must be detected, not tolerated.

args: process.stdout.write('FAIL  config file missing\nFAIL  schema file missing\n');process.exit(1);

cases.name: extra-warn-on-right
cases.description: Right emits an additional WARN the left side never produced.

args: process.stdout.write('WARN  deprecated flag used\nWARN  legacy path used\n');process.exit(0);

cases.name: same-text-different-level
cases.description: Identical message text, but FAIL on the left and WARN on the right — a severity change must not normalize away.

cases.name: diagnostic-text-differs
cases.description: Same level, same exit code, but the message text itself differs between the two sides.

cases.name: duplicate-diagnostic-only-left
cases.description: Left repeats the same WARN twice, right emits it once — a lost duplicate must be detected, not deduplicated away.

args: process.stdout.write('WARN  legacy path used\nWARN  legacy path used\n');process.exit(0);

cases.name: spawn-error-on-right
cases.description: Right side names a command that cannot be found — this must surface as an explicit harness refusal, never as a match and never as an ordinary divergence.

cases.name: intentional-divergence-proof
cases.description: Deliberately obvious mismatch (a FAIL and a non-zero exit on one side against silent success on the other), included specifically to prove the mechanism raises a divergence rather than staying silent on any input.

cases.name: unparseable-diagnostic-like-line
cases.description: Both sides print an identical line that starts with FAIL but does not match the strict diagnostic form — an aggressive normalizer would silently ignore it and wrongly report a match; this harness must instead refuse with an explicit harness_error.

args: process.stdout.write('FAILURE: something that looks like a diagnostic but is not\n');process.exit(1);
process.stdout.write('FAILURE: something that looks like a diagnostic but is not\n');process.exit(1);

cases.name: real-node-rust-source-format-adapters
cases.description: The actual frozen Node.js YAML/JSON Schema implementation and the actual Rust adapters evaluate the same adversarial corpus.

cases.name: real-node-rust-regions-adapters
cases.description: Package meridian-cli-foundation, subpackage validate-mechanical-integrity, third CHANGES_REQUESTED round, item 1: the actual frozen scripts/lib/regions.mjs (blankFencedBlocks/markedRegion/instructionRegions) and the actual compiled meridian_app::source_format::regions functions (blank_fenced_blocks/marked_region/instruction_regions) evaluate the same shared positive/adversarial corpus (verification/conformance-harness/fixtures/regions-corpus.json) — Unicode/Cyrillic before and inside a fence/region, Front Matter, CRLF, short/long/nested/unclosed fences, duplicate/missing/reversed markers, a duplicated region id, and sourceText preservation. Both producers call the real exported/compiled functions directly, never a test-only copy. blank_fenced_blocks's own raw blanked-whitespace WIDTH is deliberately normalized away by both producers before comparison (collapsed to one placeholder per run) — an intentional, documented boundary: Node blanks one space per UTF-16 code unit, Rust blanks one space per UTF-8 byte (required so later byte offsets used to slice the original raw text stay valid), and nothing downstream of either language's own blanked buffer ever inspects that width. Every other observation (which lines are blanked at all, error text, region text/attrs, instruction-region ids/owners/generated/text/sourceText, uncoveredLines) is compared verbatim.

cases.name: real-node-rust-rule-resolution
cases.description: The actual frozen Node.js resolver and the actual Rust application adapter resolve the same shared corpus.

cases.name: real-node-rust-cli-resolve
cases.description: Package meridian-cli-foundation, item 2: the actual frozen Node.js resolver and the actual compiled `meridian` binary's `resolve` subcommand (spawned as a real subprocess per request, request piped on stdin — meridian-cli/examples/resolve_cli_producer.rs) resolve the same shared corpus. Distinct from real-node-rust-rule-resolution above, which only reaches meridian-app in-process.

cases.name: real-node-rust-cli-validate-clean-kernel
cases.description: Package meridian-cli-foundation, item 2: the actual frozen Node.js scripts/kernel-validate.mjs and the actual compiled `meridian` binary's `validate` subcommand — spawned as a real subprocess by meridian-cli/examples/validate_cli_producer.rs, which only reformats that subprocess's own real --format json stdout into FAIL/WARN lines, never calling collect_diagnostics or any other library function itself — evaluate the real, current Kernel checkout. expected_status is deliberately "divergent", not "conformant": `meridian validate` correctly refuses exit code 0 while any BLOCKED_CHECKS family remains unported (item 1 of the second CHANGES_REQUESTED round), so its exit code legitimately differs from the complete Node reference's even on an otherwise-clean tree with zero real FAIL/WARN differences. test/conformance-harness.test.mjs additionally asserts the exact shape of this expected divergence (exit_code.match: false, but empty fail/warn missing/added on both sides) — a plain expected_status: "divergent" alone would not catch a regression that also broke diagnostic-content agreement.
